title: Introduce signal-conflux aggregator and alert-phasing controller
author: Maya Lin
release_notes: Adds Signal Conflux aggregator for multi-signal drift detection, a phased alert suppression controller, and a multi-signal overlay dashboard. Opt-in via observability.conflux.enabled; includes runbook and playbook examples.
description:
Motivation: We observe correlated but noisy signal changes across metrics, traces and logs that individually trigger noisy alerts. This PR introduces a Signal Conflux aggregator that fuses metric/tracing/log signals into compact drift events, and an Alert Phasing controller that stages suppression windows based on drift confidence. Goals: reduce alert churn from transient cross-signal noise, provide a single correlated drift artifact for downstream playbooks (alerting, incident-bot), and surface a multi-signal overlay dashboard for SRE/SE debugging.

What this PR changes (high level):
- telemetry/aggregator: adds signal_conflux service that consumes metric time-series (prometheus-derived), trace-derived latency histograms, and log-derived entropy scores to produce a unified drift event with confidence bands.
- alerts/phasing: adds phased_suppression controller policy that consults the drift event and tenant-configured tolerances to apply graduated suppressions (quiet, delayed, escalate).
- dashboards/multi_signal_overlay: a new Grafana panel JSON that overlays normalized metric z-score, trace p95 delta, and log-entropy sparkline with an annotated drift timeline.
- tracing/sidecar: adds a lightweight sidecar enrichment hook to attach drift-event id to sampled traces (for quick join in the UI).
- runbooks/playbooks: adds playbook and runbook docs describing how to tune phasing windows and how to interpret the overlay.
- e2e tests: adds synthetic multi-signal replay harness for regression and an integration test that verifies suppression behavior under staged drifts.

Compatibility and rollout: the feature is behind a per-cluster feature flag (observability.conflux.enabled) and per-tenant knobs (conflux.tolerance, phasing.window_ms). Default configs leave behavior disabled to avoid surprise changes. Rollout plan: enable in canary clusters with conservative tolerances, monitor alert volume and false-suppressions for 72h, then expand to production.

Design notes:
- Aggregation is intentionally lightweight: signals are normalized and downsampled to 1s resolution before fusion; we keep a fixed-size ring buffer to bound memory. Confidence bands use a simple exponential-decay ensemble instead of full Bayesian inference for predictability at scale.
- Phasing controller applies three stages: 1) quiet window (silence non-actionable low-confidence alerts), 2) delayed escalation (batch actionable alerts for a delay window), 3) forced escalation (if confidence rises). Each stage is configurable and recorded as tags on emitted alerts.

Testing and verification:
- unit tests for aggregator normalization and envelope generation.
- integration test in CI (observability-integration) that replays a synthetic drift trace and asserts: (a) one consolidated drift-event created, (b) non-actionable alerts suppressed in stage 1, (c) staged escalation executed when confidence increases.
- manual validation: ran canary in staging for 48h and observed a 38% reduction in duplicate-alerts for a sample customer workload while preserving incident captures for true regressions.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files field.

Related work: builds on ENG-1124 (metric-fusion proto) and ENG-1156 (alert-rate controller). Also references SUP-3421 for customer-reported noisy alerting.

Operational runbook excerpt (short):
- If alerts appear missing: toggle observability.conflux.log_level=debug and check /internal/observability/conflux/events for recently produced drift-events.
- To revert quickly: set observability.conflux.enabled=false per-cluster.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Long-term: consider a more expressive causal model for cross-signal correlation (future work).
- UX: explore a compact drift-event index for quick lookup in the Console (follow-up PR).

Summary: This PR centralizes noisy signal correlations into a single artifact and provides a configurable staged suppression mechanism that reduces alert fatigue while preserving SLO-relevant signals. The change is opt-in, covered by tests and runbooks, and was merged after a short canary period.
